changes.summary: Imported the M3 Wave 3 overlay/layer primitive batch (Tooltip, Popover, HoverCard, DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, Menubar) for task 4.4. None of these six items actually depend on upstream's portal.rs or a JS positioning engine (only toast.rs uses the portal in the real upstream source, contrary to the earlier migration-queue speculation drawn from inventory metadata alone) -- positioning is pure CSS via `data-side`/`data-align` attributes, already representable with the crate-root ContentSide/ContentAlign enums ported alongside this batch. Trigger components no longer depend on upstream's separate `dioxus-attributes` proc-macro crate or its `merge_attributes` helper or the polymorphic `r#as` render prop; default behavioral attributes are written directly on each trigger element with `..props.attributes` spread after them, the same plain-spread pattern this crate's `dialog` module already established. Popover's and ContextMenu's inline `document::eval` focus-trap/scroll-lock scripts are replaced with this crate's existing target-gated `use_focus_trap`/`FocusTrapScript`/new per-component gated helpers, keeping every module SSR-safe by construction instead of relying on an unconditional `document::eval` call. ContextMenu's long-press timer uses this crate's own target-aware `time::sleep` instead of upstream's `dioxus_sdk_time` dependency. DropdownMenu, ContextMenu, and Menubar reuse the collection/selectable roving-focus infrastructure already imported for Select; no new shared collection primitive was needed. Verified for native (SSR-safe default), `--features web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`, and `--features desktop`.

Real-browser testing (a live `dx serve` fixture plus Playwright) surfaced that this crate's long-lived, repeatedly-firing `document::eval` listener pattern -- `use_global_escape_listener` and `use_outside_dismiss` in lib.rs, both inherited unmodified from the M1 Dialog/Select fork -- never actually registers its `document.addEventListener` call in this Dioxus 0.7.9/0.7.10 web runtime (confirmed by instrumenting `document.addEventListener` itself: the count stays zero after opening a Popover). The one-shot request/response `document::eval` pattern (`use_animated_open`'s exit-animation wait) does work, isolating the gap to the long-lived listen-repeatedly pattern specifically. `dialog`'s existing browser tests never actually exercised this path: DialogRoot's Escape handling is a native Dioxus onkeydown on its own root element, and the registry facade's outside-dismiss is a native onclick on its full-screen overlay div, not `use_outside_dismiss`. Popover has no such overlay and was the first primitive to depend solely on the broken path, so PopoverRoot now also carries a native onkeydown Escape handler (same reliable mechanism as dialog). Outside-dismiss and focus-trapping for popover/context-menu remain dependent on the unverified eval path pending a root-cause fix (tracked as a follow-up, likely M6 shared-primitive-expansion territory since it affects the shared lib.rs listener helpers, not just this batch); the Wave 3 Playwright suite asserts only the behavior confirmed to work in the browser (open/close, native-keyboard Escape and roving focus, hover/focus triggers, ARIA roles) rather than claiming untested coverage.

Re-authored packages/adico-primitives/src/tooltip.rs, popover.rs, and hover_card.rs per openspec/changes/reauthor-primitives-from-independent-spec task 5.5. No logic changes to any of the three -- all already independently structured and already correctly delegating to the shared Positioner and (for popover.rs) the shared focus-trap/escape-key helpers. dropdown_menu.rs, context_menu.rs, and menubar.rs are NOT touched by this task -- they remain blocked pending task 2.3's menu-family re-authoring onto menu::Menu, itself pending a user design decision about a new active-vs-merely-mounted layer primitive -- so this record stays open with those three files until that work lands. tooltip.rs: derived from the WAI-ARIA APG Tooltip pattern (aria-describedby-linked role=tooltip content, shown on hover/focus, dismissed on Escape), already implemented. popover.rs: no dedicated APG 'Popover' pattern exists; spec is the closest APG guidance (the Dialog pattern) applied conditionally on is_modal -- role=dialog with aria-modal/focus-trap only when modal, a non-modal disclosure otherwise -- already implemented. hover_card.rs: no dedicated APG 'Hover Card' pattern exists either; spec is the Tooltip pattern's hover/focus-triggered aria-describedby shape, with an intentional, pre-existing divergence (interactive content, stays open while hovered) the ARIA tooltip role's own spec discourages for this content shape -- documented as deliberate, not a gap. All three had zero tests; added 12 across three new files (open/closed data-state, role/aria-modal/aria-describedby, disabled propagation, PopoverContent's is_modal-conditional aria-modal). Positioner's own data-side/data-align attributes and tooltip.rs's TooltipContent-to-TooltipTrigger aria-describedby id match are both real-DOM-measurement/use_effect-driven and not assertable under a bare rebuild_in_place() -- the same effect-driven-state limitation this change has documented elsewhere -- so tests assert presence/role/state, not the exact linked id, where that gap applies. Writing hover_card.rs's tests surfaced a real, previously-undocumented interaction: HoverCardContent's force_mount prop (default true) only bypasses its own early !is_open && !force_mount return; every path still ends at use_animated_open's render() gate, and neither its SSR-fallback implementation (returns open unmodified) nor its web/native one (show_in_dom() || animating(), where animating is set nowhere) ever honors force_mount, so a closed HoverCard's content does not actually stay mounted on any target even with force_mount: true -- contradicting this file's own HoverCardContentProps::force_mount doc comment. Documented in the file's own header and in the test rather than silently worked around or fixed (fixing risks altering unrelated animation-close timing). No consumer in this repo sets force_mount: true to rely on the behavior -- registry/ui/hover_card.rs's styled facade explicitly sets force_mount: false, itself under a comment describing the same mistaken belief the primitive's own doc comment states (checked via grep across registry/, apps/, examples/, tests/installation/). Full baseline green; provenance count reduced by 3 source units (this record's remaining originalPaths/localPaths now cover only dropdown_menu.rs/context_menu.rs/menubar.rs, still blocked); registry validate/build unaffected (46 items, same accepted static-pointer pattern as prior Wave E tasks); no dedicated tests/installation/wave3-overlays-consumer fixture exists for this batch (unlike Wave E's earlier tasks), so wasm32 coverage relied on cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown against the adico-primitives crate itself plus the existing apps/playground and examples/* consumers already exercised by cargo check --locked --workspace.
